# Example data: Hermit warbler point counts (SIMULATED)

**These data are simulated.** They were generated by `dev/nmixture/make_example.R`
(seed 20250512) so that the true answer is known. No real birds were counted. The
true values are listed at the end of this file; the fit is checked against them.

## The story

A field crew surveyed breeding **Hermit warblers** (*Setophaga occidentalis*) in
conifer forest of the Oregon Coast Range in spring 2025. They placed 120 survey
points across a range of canopy cover and elevation. Each point was visited up to
three times between mid-May and mid-June, roughly two weeks apart. On each visit an
observer stood at the point and counted every Hermit warbler seen or heard.

The crew wants to know:

- how many Hermit warblers there are at the 120 points, allowing for birds that were
  present but not counted;
- whether abundance is associated with canopy cover and elevation.

Counts miss birds. A warbler singing high in the canopy on a windy morning is easy to
miss. Because each point was counted more than once, the N-mixture model can separate
"how many birds are there" from "what share of them gets counted on one visit".

## Design

| dimension | value |
|---|---|
| survey points (sites) | 120 |
| visits per point | up to 3 (346 of 360 possible visits done; 14 third visits, 3.9%, were skipped) |
| season | 10 May to 13 June 2025 (day of year 130-164) |
| observers | 3 (codes JDK, MLR, SAT) |
| population assumed closed | yes, within the season (no births, deaths or movement between visits) |

## Files

### `point_counts.csv` (one row per visit done; 346 rows)

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `point` | point identifier, `PT-001` to `PT-120` |
| `visit` | visit number at that point: 1, 2 or 3 |
| `date` | survey date (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `julian_day` | day of year of the survey (130-164) |
| `start_time` | start time of the count (HH:MM); recorded but not used in the model |
| `wind_beaufort` | wind force on the Beaufort scale, 0 (calm) to 4 |
| `observer` | observer code: JDK, MLR or SAT |
| `count` | number of Hermit warblers counted on that visit (whole number, 0 or more) |

### `points.csv` (one row per point; 120 rows)

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `point` | point identifier (matches `point_counts.csv`) |
| `canopy_cover_pct` | canopy cover at the point, % (16-98) |
| `elevation_m` | elevation, metres (152-1098) |
| `stand_type` | young / mature / old; recorded but not used (it had no effect in the simulation) |

### `config.yaml`

Tells ecotools which file and column is which, and which model to fit:
abundance depends on canopy cover and elevation, detection depends on wind, day of
year and observer, Poisson abundance, 300 bootstrap replicates for the goodness-of-fit test.

### `recovery.yaml`

The planted-truth check at this design (120 points, 3 visits, 3.9% visits missing,
the true values below). See `WALKTHROUGH.md`.

## TRUE values (simulated; known only because we made the data)

How the data were generated (`dev/nmixture/make_example.R`):

- Abundance at each point: N ~ Poisson(lambda), with
  log(lambda) = log(2.2) + 0.022 x (canopy - 62) + 0.0006 x (elevation - 600).
- Each bird present is counted on a visit with probability p, with
  logit(p) = logit(0.55) - 0.45 x (wind - 1.5) - 0.02 x (day - 145) - 0.4 x [observer is SAT].
  JDK and MLR have the same detection.
- Third visits skipped at random with probability 0.12.

The same truth on the scale the report uses (per 1 SD of each covariate, at average
covariate values; computed by `dev/nmixture/si_truth.R`, saved in
`results/nmixture/si/truth.csv`):

| quantity | true value |
|---|---|
| total Hermit warblers at the 120 points (realised) | **273** |
| mean per point (realised) | 2.275 |
| expected abundance at a point of average canopy (60.0%) and elevation (599 m) | 2.10 |
| canopy effect, log scale per SD (19.74 %) | 0.434 (rate ratio 1.54) |
| elevation effect, log scale per SD (294 m) | 0.176 (rate ratio 1.19) |
| detection per bird per visit, observer JDK, average wind (1.41) and day (146.4) | 0.553 |
| wind effect on detection, logit per SD (1.10 Beaufort) | -0.496 (odds ratio 0.61) |
| day-of-year effect on detection, logit per SD (11.5 days) | -0.230 (odds ratio 0.79) |
| observer MLR vs JDK (logit) | 0 (odds ratio 1) |
| observer SAT vs JDK (logit) | -0.40 (odds ratio 0.67) |

Other facts about the simulated population: 19 of the 120 points had no warblers; the
largest number at one point was 8; the sum over points of the largest count at each
point is 217, so the counts alone miss about 20% of the birds even on each point's best visit.
